title: U.S. Navy Task Force 59's Saronic Corsair unmanned surface vessel picked up the two crew of an Army AH-64 Apache shot down off Oman near the Strait of Hormuz and carried them to a helicopter hoist within about two hours (8–9 June 2026)
summary: Task Force 59's Corsair sea drone picked up two Apache crew shot down off Oman and took them to a helicopter hoist within about two hours.
account: At 7:33 p.m. EDT on 8 June 2026, 9 June in Oman's time zone, a U.S. Army AH-64 Apache patrolling near the Strait of Hormuz went down off Oman. President Trump said Iranian forces shot it down. U.S. Central Command said a Navy Corsair unmanned surface vessel located the two crew, who boarded it. The vessel was built by Saronic and fielded by Task Force 59 since late March. It carried them to a point on the water where a helicopter hoisted them for onward transport. CENTCOM said both were rescued within approximately two hours and were in stable condition. It said the Corsair was the closest and quickest asset. Officials called it the first real-world aircrew recovery by an unmanned surface vessel.
purpose: Saronic describes the Corsair as a 24-foot multi-mission autonomous surface vessel. gCaptain lists its design missions as maritime security, surveillance, force protection and logistics. Task Force 59 fielded it from late March 2026 to extend CENTCOM's maritime domain awareness. Recovering downed aircrew is not a stated mission. CENTCOM's spokesman said such sea drones had been used in exercises but not in real life. He said the Corsair was chosen because it was the closest and quickest asset. The benefit was an improvised use of a surveillance and logistics platform rather than its built purpose.
system: Saronic Corsair unmanned (autonomous) surface vessel operated by U.S. 5th Fleet's Task Force 59
model_version: Corsair, 24-foot diesel-powered autonomous surface vessel; Saronic specifications cited by DefenseScoop: speeds above 35 knots, 1,000 lb payload over 1,000 nautical miles, 360-degree passive sensing for day and night; gCaptain: radar, cameras, satellite communications, onboard computing and autonomous navigation software; no software version reported
deployer: U.S. Navy, 5th Fleet Task Force 59 (U.S. Naval Forces Central Command)
location: Off the coast of Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz
domain: Military search and rescue / personnel recovery at sea
segment: Government, security, and defense (naval unmanned surface vessels)
taxonomy_note: An at-sea rescue of aircrew is read as a health outcome because no rescue type exists.

ratings.reason: Two unnamed Army aviators were shot down at night in a conflict zone. They were taken out of the water within about two hours and reached a helicopter. CENTCOM said they were in stable condition, and Trump said both were safe and uninjured. No source shows they were in imminent danger of drowning or capture, or that no other asset could have reached them. A life-saving effect is not established.

The Army got its two aviators back within about two hours, using what CENTCOM's spokesman called the closest and quickest asset. CENTCOM publicized the operation as the first real-world recovery of aircrew by an unmanned surface vessel. gCaptain calls it a significant operational milestone for Task Force 59 and for Saronic, six months after a $392 million Navy production contract.

ai_role.statement: Saronic and gCaptain describe the Corsair as an autonomous surface vessel with autonomous navigation software. It can run under remote supervision or autonomously, and Task Force 59 is the Navy's unit for unmanned systems and artificial intelligence. CENTCOM says the drone located and picked up the crew and carried them to a hoist point. No cited source states whether it navigated autonomously or was remotely supervised during the recovery. None states how it found the two men or what its sensors contributed. DefenseScoop's remark that the 360-degree sensing likely helped is the reporter's inference. The hoist and onward transport were done by a crewed helicopter. Nextgov reports that U.S. Naval Forces Central Command, the 82nd Airborne Division and Air Force and Navy units assisted in the rescue.

produced_by: A Corsair unmanned surface vessel already fielded in theater by Task Force 59 since late March 2026. It was close enough to the crash site to be, in CENTCOM's words, the closest and quickest asset
A crewed helicopter able to hoist the crew from the vessel at a second point on the water and carry them onward
Two aviators who survived the shoot-down uninjured and could board a 24-foot vessel from the water
must_hold: The vessel must reach the crew before exposure or hostile forces do. Here recovery took about two hours, and the sources do not say how close Iranian forces were
Someone must still complete the rescue chain, here a helicopter hoist and onward transport

The vessel's navigation and sensing must work in a contested strait. The House Armed Services Committee noted the same week that navigation jamming and cut communications with crewed ships are to be expected
